notes.title: AETHUS joins Tiny Teams 2025!
notes.content:
Hello again, Pioneers! 
I'm delighted to announce that AETHUS is featured in this year’s Tiny Teams festival, organised by YogsCast!

I'm super excited to be joining the lineup of awesome games made by other micro-sized developers this year, and I'm hugely proud that AETHUS was selected from over 2,000 other applicants to be featured!

Huge thanks to the YogsCast crew for their trust and belief in the game and I!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/83461d4d8f3a086935b2e2adf49daa2dbe6ef22f.jpg"]

As part of the fest, be sure to check out the free demo for AETHUS!

I've worked hard to ensure the demo provides the best possible intro to AETHUS for new players, so if you’re jumping into the game for the first time, welcome! It's great to have you! 
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2822250/AETHUS_Demo/"][/dynamiclink]About my Tiny Team - Pawsmonaut Games
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/bde849a681c09b72aee20c5c1cabd06c5e1562b7.png"]If you're new around here, let me introduce myself! 

I'm Alex, and I'm the solo-dev behind AETHUS, and my microstudio, Pawsmonaut Games.

I named my studio after my dog, a dalmatian named Apollo. You may be able to tell that space and sci-fi have always been close to my heart in my choice of names (and debut game genre and setting!).

I am the only person working on the game day-to-day, which means I have full control over everything - just the way I like it! Quality and attention to detail are my top priorities when making the game, so I'm always striving to make sure everything I do hits the mark.

I have some awesome freelance partners who contribute in areas like audio design, music, artwork and narrative design, but Apollo and I are the only ones with access to the game project files and everything goes through us!

I worked on AAA games at studios like Rockstar North, Build a Rocket Boy and Splash Damage before going indie and forming Pawsmonaut in 2023 to make games a bit differently - with AAA quality and attention to detail, but indie heart. No predatory business practices or microtransactions, openness and honesty in communication, and absolutely no AI content!


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/09e597ab0c17828f504048c54dd7142497c82c71.png"]
I hope this little insight into the studio gives you a bit more info on who's making AETHUS, and I'd love to chat further about the game or studio in the Pawsmonaut Discord. 

Join the Discord

Join the community and talk to me directly, get access to future playtests for the game, and get exclusive behind-the-scenes content!
Reminder: Gameplay Deep Dive
If you're new here or missed it, I recently released the first Gameplay Deep Dive for AETHUS which I titled 'The Menagerie'![dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mwV-Qga2G64"][/dynamiclink]Join me as I take you through various game features and introduce you to Trudy - your corporate rep - as we work to populate a corporate menagerie by collecting some mysterious eggs and earn some extra credits for our effort! 

Remember, you can check out the demo during Tiny Teams 2025 and if you enjoy what you play, please leave a review! The more positive reviews we can gather, the more new people we can introduce to the game!


[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2822250/AETHUS_Demo/"][/dynamiclink]And thanks again to everyone who’s reviewed the demo already! <3 

Have an awesome Tiny Teams Fest!

notes.title: Gameplay Deep Dive #1 & Publishing Update
notes.content:
Hello again, Pioneers! I hope you're having a lovely summer!Gameplay Deep Dive
I'm pleased to present the very first Gameplay Deep Dive - 'The Menagerie'!

In this video, come with me as I take you through various game features as you get your first introduction to Trudy, we work to populate a corporate menagerie by collecting some mysterious eggs, and earn some extra credits for our effort! 

[dynamiclink href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mwV-Qga2G64"][/dynamiclink]Let me know what you think of this Deep Dive in the comments or via social media or Discord!

If you enjoyed it and would like to see more, I'd love to know what you'd enjoy a Deep Dive to focus on.


If you like what you've seen and haven't done so yet, you can go ahead and try out the free demo! 
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/2822250/AETHUS_Demo/"][/dynamiclink]Publishing Update
If you were paying attention in the last month or so, you'll have seen an update about AETHUS being published by CULT Games.

I wanted to update you all to let you know that this won't be moving forward and AETHUS will continue to be fully indie and self-published. I retain full control over every aspect of the game and its IP.

This decision was a difficult one to make, but I now firmly believe that the best path forward for the game is to be completely independent. 

Rest assured that the game is coming along incredibly well, and I will be running the final playtest of the game in the next couple of months!

What this does mean though is that I will need your help more than ever in spreading the word about the game, sharing content like the Deep Dive above with people you think might enjoy it, and making sure you Wishlist and Follow the game.



If you've played the demo and enjoyed it, I'd really (really!) appreciate it if you would drop even just a couple of lines as a review on the demo page - it really helps with visibility!



Thanks as always for your support in making AETHUS as successful as it can be! <3



As always, until next time!

Alex and Apollo.

notes.title: AETHUS x CULT Games - Publishing Announcement
notes.content:
Hello again, Pioneers!I’m super excited to share that I have joined forces with CULT Games, who will publish AETHUS and bring it to a much wider audience than I could achieve on my own!
As a solo-indie developer this partnership will allow me to focus all of my energy on creating the best game possible, and not need to spend time and effort on all the other bits that go along with it - marketing, social media, business relationships, press, etc.

CULT really ‘get’ the game and I’m super excited to be working with them.


I wanted to share some words from Sarah, brand manager for the game at CULT, who you will be hearing more from (along with others!) in the near future:

“Hey Pioneers, just popping my head out of the dev cave to say: AETHUS is a beautiful, soulful game and we love it. We love you for loving it as much as we do. We're here to champion and protect its anti-corporate heart. Please keep talking at Alex and the team at CULT about what you want and think of AETHUS. We’re listening (and also probably lasering scrap at 3am). Really looking forward to spending time with the community and seeing you all play the finished game this year.”


I also want to make it clear that I still have full creative control over all aspects of the game, and I was very careful in choosing a partner who totally respects that and trusts me to deliver on my strong vision with no compromises.

Long story short - this partnership will make the game better. Simple as that.

You can check out the new trailer for the game below, and if you haven’t already, please do wishlist the game - it helps a huge amount! 
[previewyoutube="uszrU89pgmc;full"][/previewyoutube]
The new demo for the game is also available and ready for you to play, and I’d love to hear any feedback or suggestions you might have. It’s genuinely really important to me.

Speak soon, Pioneers!

Alex, Apollo, and CULT Games

notes.title: May 2025 Development Diary
notes.content:
Hello again, Pioneers!

Welcome to the May Development Diary for AETHUS!

This month, we recap on the May Playtest, cover the new Demo Update and check out a rework of the Power System based on feedback!

May Development

May Playtest
The May Playtest mentioned in the last devlog has now concluded, and once again was hugely successful!

A vast amount of excellent feedback was obtained, and over the two weeks of the playtest I worked very closely with the testers to iterate on features, balancing, new content and fix lots of (small!) bugs!

I'm very proud to say that the average enjoyment score for the game was 8.8/10 after leaving feedback!

The game is better than ever thanks to the help of our excellent playtesters, so I want to thank them all again for their help making the game the best it can be!

There will be one final large-scale playtest before launch, coming in the next few months, so if you'd like the chance to take part make sure you join the Discord and become part of the community!

Demo Update
What's Changed?
Eagle-eyed community members spotted that the demo for the game received an update last week, so I wanted to let you know what changed!

This update brings the demo build up to quality parity with the rest of the game (as of the end of the May Playtest), including some new content with a slightly reworked early-game, new Settings and Options (and keybinds!), and brand new QOL features with keybinds + buttons such as:

 Inventory Auto-Stack
 Deposit Refinable Items
 Deposit All Items
 Take All Items
and more!

Overall, this update is intended to make the demo the best possible intro to the game it can be for new players as we move forward towards release!

Demo Steam Page
As part of this update, I also swapped the demo to a separate Steam page!
This means that you can now leave reviews directly for the demo, which helps give new potential players an idea of what people thing and make an informed choice!

It would help me out a lot if you'd take a couple of minutes to head to the Demo Page and leave a review if you enjoyed it, even if it was a while ago! The more positive reviews we can gather, the more new people we can introduce the game to!

Thanks a lot to those who've already left reviews, it really does help and means a lot to me as a solo developer! ❤

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2822250/AETHUS_Demo/
Power System Rework
November's Playtest brought up a bunch of feedback about the Power System in the game - some testers enjoyed it, but several found it a little confusing and potentially restricting.

OLD SYSTEM:
There were two 'Power' systems in play at once:

OUTPOST POWER
An overall power level of your base, simply the amount of power generation you have minus the amount of power consumption you have (from facilities). 
If Outpost Power hit zero, facilities would stop working and you'd need to build more power generation.

POWER SLOTS
Each Habitat had a certain amount of 'Power Slots' available, and each Facility you built would take up a certain amount of them, depending on its size. 
If a Habitat didn't have enough 'Power Slots' available, you couldn't build a Facility that took up more than was available. 

For example, the Basic Habitat had six 'Power Slots', while the Crafting Bench took up two. If you were already using five slots in the Hab, you couldn't build a Crafting Bench in there.

The motive behind this system was to essentially force you to expand the Outpost, create new Habitats, and unlock bigger and better ones as you progress in the game which support more Power Slots.

NEW SYSTEM:
OUTPOST POWER
Unchanged (subject to changes in the future around progression of generation types!)

POWER SLOTS
Removed. You can now build as many facilities in each Habitat as you can physically fit!

The removal of Power Slots both makes Power much simpler and easier to understand (no confusion between Power and Power Slots), and allows you more freedom and creativity. If you want to try and fit every facility into one Hab, who am I to stop you!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/614e972c35051e720a30269195ad01dfc6393008.png
HAB BONUSES
I do still want to encourage you to expand your Outpost, so to do this I've created a new incentive system - Hab Bonuses.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/9c226c8316ce2986e8cba83f3b8ae880735a03a8.png
As you progress through the game, you will unlock new types of Habitats with Hab Bonuses - these are powerful benefits which the Hab provides you when used. 

As an example - the Greenhouse Hab; hydroponic crops grown within it will often create produce extra resources!

You can still grow things in any other Hab, but it's a powerful bonus and worth expanding your Outpost with a Greenhouse Hab if you intend to grow crops!

If you have ideas for Hab Bonuses you'd like to see, why not drop a comment and I'll add the best ones to the game! 👇

That's it for this development diary! Remember to take just a minute to head to the demo page and leave a review and help me out! ❤

Until next time,
Alex (and Apollo)

notes.title: April 2025 Development Diary
notes.content:
Hello again, Pioneers!

Welcome to the April Development Diary for AETHUS!

I know, I missed the dev diary for March, again, my bad!
Things have been incredibly busy preparing for the next Playtest, which is scheduled for early May - there will be a full 2/3 of the game playable from start to finish, so if you're keen to take a sneak-peek, head over to the Discord where sign-ups will be happening in the very near future!

I also have a big announcement coming up that should mean a lot more getting shared with you over the coming months, but we're not quite ready to talk about it yet... It won't be too long, though!

April Development

Intro Animatic
If you've played the demo of the game, you've probably noticed the click-to-progress text-scrawl at the start before you get into the game - it's always just been a placeholder to set some context for the characters and story, but it's always bugged me because it looks a bit rubbish! Well...

Presenting the Intro Animatic!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/2a6063424c3b772c9e331e52c5f22c061ccffe10.png
This is just one (unanimated!) shot from the brand new fully-voiced-over and very fancy Animatic which will feature as the new intro to the game, giving you a good dose of world context as well as story, character and narrative setup as you start the game!

The new Intro Animatic will feature in the upcoming playtest as well as appearing as a standalone cinematic trailer in the coming months, so once again, get involved if you'd like a sneak-peek!

Prospecting
Prospecting is a system you'll unlock partway through the game, which allows you to collect and then Prospect valuable geodes that you can find when out mining in the world!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/3b09298c00932582ab17b271a79edeffcabc4745.png
Via a minigame, you'll use the Prospecting Bench's laser to chip away at the geodes you load into it, to uncover whatever's hidden inside - this could be high quality ore, gems, or even special collectible items...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/20691d066f2ac6ba8f02a52a8274b2cdb9e30534.png
Unlock Upgrades and find items through exploration that can improve your Prospecting abilities as you advance through the game, to make sure that you always end up with the maximum yield from your finds!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/f96e88826d9bedb54614aea8fa72596de69a14ff.png
Graphics Settings
Providing a diverse set of game settings for you all is important to me, so that you can tailor the experience of the game to your preference - that goes for gameplay settings as demonstrated in previous dev diaries, but also for graphics settings!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/9dcf246317735080656966f8e67fd98ef34e9b31.png
I've recently added support for a bunch of new settings related to Image Scaling/Anti-Aliasing, including the following technologies:

 FXAA/TAA/MSAA/TSR
 NVIDIA DLSS/DLAA
 NVIDIA Image Scaling
In addition, you can increase and decrease the resolution scaling of the game manually when using one of the Built-In AA technologies or NVIDIA Image Scaling on 'Custom' Mode.

Finally, I have also added support for DLSS Frame Generation, including 4x FrameGen for those with the supported newer cards.

Are there any other graphics settings or technologies you'd like to see implemented? Leave a comment below! 👇

May Playtest
As mentioned at the start of the dev diary, the next playtest for AETHUS will begin in early May.
Signups will go live on the Discord next week, so if you're keen to see the post-demo areas of the game, join us over there for a chance at advanced playtesting!

The last playtest was a huge success and made for excellent feedback and changes to the game, and I'm very confident that this will be the same - another step closer to release!

That's it for this development diary!

Until next time,
Alex (and Apollo)

notes.title: AETHUS - February Development Diary
notes.content:
Hello again, Pioneers!

Welcome to the February Development Diary for AETHUS!

You may have noticed there wasn't a January Development Diary - apologies for that, but there just wasn't that much of interest to show at the start of the year while lots happens in the background and just general work on the game continues!

We're back now though, and have a couple of things to share!

February Development

New Key Art
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/396881a252497e670b43b92c7bc47d40a16ab650.png
You may have already noticed from the cover image of this post, but AETHUS now has new key art!

As we ramp up towards launch this year, I wanted new key art and Steam capsules (which are also already live, check them out!) which better represent the themes of the game and try to make it clear what type of game this is - a survival-crafter, all about exploration, mystery and discovery!

I hope you love the new art as much as I do, I'd love to hear your thoughts, either on Discord or in the comments!

The Magma Rifts
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/2d82e085c7ddb60bcdc654887dd7afc8dd83bbfe.jpg
Here's the final biome of the game, at the border of the very mantle of Aethus itself... the Magma Rifts.

What's that weird floating crystal? What kind of resources await you here? What kind of mysteries lie in wait?... All will be revealed!

Loading Times
A small but important one - you'll be coming and going from the caverns and underground of Aethus very frequently, and it's important that your time isn't wasted while doing so.

To that end, I've recently been optimising the level loading/unloading and related functionality to make sure that this process is as quick as possible, getting you out of black-screen-fades more swiftly and back to doing what you do best - gathering resources and building your Outpost!

So far, after a first optimisation pass, I've managed to improve loading times by 25-30% over previous (e.g. in the Demo).

There's always more work to be done, but from playtesting I've already noticed a big difference!

That's it for this development diary!

Next month may well have some very exciting news to share, that's been a long time in the making...

Until next time,
Alex (and Apollo)

notes.title: AETHUS - December Development Diary
notes.content:
Hello again, Pioneers!

Welcome to the December Development Diary for AETHUS!

Happy holiday season to you, but particularly I want to wish you a Merry Christmas, from my Outpost to yours! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/d3fbc4447f681b45e4a33bd8e72b6b643c07944e.png

This month has been a busy one, with a lot of exciting things going on behind the scenes that I can't talk about or show yet, but I wanted to give you a couple of updates on some small things to tide you over this festive season!

December Development

The Lost World
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/b54324833e5d5c7de1fb944ba397c398b2dd932a.png
This is a real advance sneak-peek as I'm still working on fully defining the final(?) visual style for this biome, but here's a shot from one sub-zone within the second biome of the game - the Lost World. Maybe this one should have been in the October dev diary... Spooky! 👻

Quality of Life Continues
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/634518de1075c8edeb384e2bf89deb3a4c0cf9c9.jpg
Whenever I get the chance, I love to add new quality of life (QOL) features to the game to make it as rewarding and friction-free as possible to play. 

This was just one example of a recent one, a great suggestion from one of the playtesting crew - resources that are used in refining for a selected facility (or required for a specific interaction, like repairing a door) are now highlighted in your inventory!

Rich Presence
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/04642afe65363face914394b542bdb58cec95d9f.png
Just a cool little thing I added this month - Steam Rich Presence support, so now when you play the game your friends will be able to keep track of your progress through the world!

That's it for this development diary!

I just want to thank everyone - playtesters, wishlisters, followers and supporters, big and small, for all your amazing help and support during 2024. It's been incredible to see the game grow and improve every day, and I can't wait to get it into your hands in 2025.

Have a restful and joyful holiday season, stay safe! See you next year.

Until next time,
Alex (and Apollo)

notes.title: AETHUS - November Development Diary
notes.content:
Hello again, Pioneers!

Welcome to the November Development Diary for AETHUS!

Happy Thanksgiving to those of you who celebrate. This month, I have an update on the ongoing Closed Playtest and some exciting development updates!

Playtesting

The November Closed Playtest is due to finish on Monday, and the response has been superb - feedback is overwhelmingly positive for this large chunk of the game, with many excellent suggestions for improvements and quality of life features submitted by playtesters, who've been enjoying the game a lot this month.

I want to thank everyone who's been helping with the playtest and providing feedback, with a special shout-out to Yugubugu, star playtester who's been practically running QA for the game this last month, putting over 70 hours into the playtest so far!

There will be future opportunities for playtesting, so keep an eye here, on the socials, or ideally the Discord to be the first to know!

November Development

Themes and Customization

While exploring the underground world of Aethus, you will eventually discover and collect Themes that you can use to customize the constructions within, and the habitats of, your Outpost.

[previewyoutube=57xltLqPZVo;full][/previewyoutube]
Themed after the Big Five megacorporations of the AETHUS lore, you can quickly and easily select items for theming, and even select a Habitat to instantly theme everything within it! 

Mix and match themes to find your perfect combination, as almost everything you construct can be themed individually!

What kind of themes would you like to see in the game? Leave a comment below!

Automation
AETHUS isn't a factory or automation game, but I definitely want you to feel the satisfaction of 'graduating' from needing to mine and gather certain basic resources early on, to automating these processes so you can focus on the deeper, cooler resources!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/8d31029fade3c622b15b53af9ef8a9f2f01a9a9f.png
To that end, one way you'll automate your resource gathering is by reactivating old automated mining drills that you find within the underground! 

 Different drills harvest different resources, in different areas.
 Find or craft drill bits to fix a drill and get it working again!
 Find or craft a Cargo Drone to enable automatic delivery of resources from the drill to special facilities within your Outpost!

That's it for this development diary - as always, thanks for your support. See you next month for the final dev diary of 2024!

Until next time,
Alex (and Apollo)

notes.title: AETHUS - October Development Diary
notes.content:
Hello, Pioneers!

Happy Samhain (Halloween) and welcome to the October Development Diary for AETHUS.

As the nights draw in and the weather gets colder here in Scotland, progress continues apace as we approach an exciting milestone - a new closed playtest of the post-demo area of the game!

If you're interested in participating and have some time to devote to doing so (and providing feedback!), please do sign up - instructions on how to do so are just past the main development updates for the month.

Finally, a big topic for discussion - the future release plans for the game next year! I'm really interested in hearing your thoughts about the options. Check it out at the end of the Diary!

October Development

User Interface Pass
A large pass on the UI for the game has just been completed which has reworked or updated most of the user interfaces across the game, including some post-demo features which previously had placeholders. 

Various post-demo features will be revealed in future development diaries, starting with the Planetary Market this month (see below) but for now, check out these before/after shots of two of the game UIs that have received attention this month!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/814a596fad3587590e733d9d73807f131e655d62.jpg
The Build UI has been reworked for clarity, readability and centralisation of important info!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/5ccd3a206ffa9cb5ae113028dcb159ea30682947.jpg
The Upgrades UI hasn't been shown before, but here's how it looked before vs now!

I'd love to hear your thoughts on these changes!

Planetary Exchange Network - the Market
The ARC Planetary Exchange Network, or the 'Market', is one of the game features you'll quickly gain access to in the game.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/d91782991c97330bda099205ef2335924218a318.png
The Market allows you to sell the resources you gather for ARC Credits, which you can use to purchase construction blueprints, crafting plans, and Upgrades for both your Mining Suit and Roland!

As you make purchases from the corporation, you'll level up in the ARC Resource Acquisition Partnership Program (RAPP) - as you do so, you'll unlock rewards like new blueprints and plans to purchase, gifts, and more!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/c9e7183efeef3d278ea8848751ae8655715802a8.png
If you're short on credits, don't worry - exploring the world will provide you with many of the blueprints and plans you can purchase on the Market! Oh, and you'll never be out of pocket - if you discover a plan or blueprint you've already purchased, you'll be reimbursed the credits! 

This is just one of the small quality-of-life features I'm prioritising in the game. 
You should never be penalised for exploring!

Playtesting Signups

I'm happy to say that development is proceeding well and I'm about ready to accept a new wave of playtesters for the next closed playtest of AETHUS!

This playtest will include the full extent of the post-demo area of the first biome in the game, the Outer Caverns, and span between 4-6 hours of gameplay in total.

You can sign up for playtesting here.

The form requires an email signup, but I promise it won't be used for anything except contacting you for this one specific playtest, and if you decide to join the Discord then please feel free to leave this empty as long as you provide your username so I can contact you!

Release Plans
In the spirit of transparency and open development (a big change from my AAA days!) I wanted to get your opinions on how AETHUS should be released.

Before I say anything else - my goal will always be to release the most high-quality and bug-free experience possible, regardless of what release plan I go for.

With that said, I had originally planned to go straight to a full, 1.0 release. For a couple of reasons, I'm now also considering the option of an Early Access release.
This is by no means decided, and I'm really keen to hear your thoughts and opinions. 

Why Early Access?
Primarily, an EA release would allow me to bring in some income (I am self-funded, no publisher, and Apollo needs to eat!) and allow you access to the game earlier at a lower price point. With money coming in, this would actually increase the budget of the game and allow me headroom to spend funds on making the game even better - higher fidelity, more content, etc.

What would it look like?
The plan would be to release into Early Access with 2/3 of the biomes in the game, which effectively also means 2/3 of the total game content. 

The target for launching into early access would be Q2 2025. 
The EA period would likely only last for ~6mo and, aside from small patches and hotfixes, would likely only contain one large content update - the final biome of the game, new systems, constructions, items, etc. and the conclusion of the story.

Whether an EA or 1.0 release plan is what I go with in the end, quality is top priority, and EA would not be an excuse or justification for releasing a more buggy or lower quality game! Nor would there be any difference in the end product, the length of the game at 1.0 will be the same regardless of EA or not.

Let me hear your thoughts!
Would you rather have the chance to play the game and support me earlier, at a lower price point, or would you rather wait a bit longer and get everything all at once? Naturally, if going the EA route, I would also be continuing to build the game with your feedback at heart, but the vision is strong, the story and world are planned out, and the high-level plans aren't likely to change.

So, all that said, I want to hear your thoughts. Please leave a comment, or join the discussion on Discord and let's chat about it. It'd be great to see you there.

That's it for this development diary - as always, thanks for your support. 

Until next time,
Alex (and Apollo)

notes.title: AETHUS - September Development Diary
notes.content:
Hello, Pioneers!

Welcome to the September Development Diary for AETHUS.

The last month was huge for the game, with the demo revamp and Steam Space Exploration Festival being a massive success, bringing thousands of new players to the game and community. 

It's been incredibly heartwarming to see the positive response to the game you've all shown, and thank you once again for providing such excellent feedback.

This month, I have updates for you on just a couple of the features I've been working on.

September Development

Gravity Tethers
[previewyoutube=1t1hjdjLZzk;full][/previewyoutube]
Roland has been outfitted with new ARC technology - Gravity Tethers!

Your sentient AI companion can now lift resources up and drag them towards you in the world, to make resource gathering that little bit easier.

Upgrade the Gravity Tethers as you progress to increase their range and speed of attraction, to the point where you can sprint around the world dragging a trail of debris behind you!

Construction Renaming
[previewyoutube=Pk7uO9YxvJg;full][/previewyoutube]
You will be able to freely rename any constructions you build within your Outpost!

Whether you want to rename your storage chests to aid in organising your supplies, or pay homage to a friend with a dedicated habitat, you can rename anything you build.

That's it for this development diary - as always, thanks for your support.

notes.title: AETHUS Demo 2.0 - 'Demo Revamp' - Now Live!
notes.content:
Patch Eleven - the 'Demo Revamp' is now live!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/e254eb61ff14ffb9e4929a570f02c2f9ced00171.png

To celebrate the Steam Space Exploration Fest, I'm delighted that Patch Eleven, a huge revamp of the AETHUS demo, is now live!

The list of changes and fixes is so large that I can't really break it down, but here are the highest level topics - if you've been waiting to try the demo, there won't be a better time until the Next Fest before release in 2025!

Patch Highlights

 Control/Key rebinding support. ⌨
 Improved character movement. 👨‍🚀
 Surface expansion (4x the size!) with new areas. 🌴🏜️
 Build Mode improvements (greater zoom out, build from storage, much better snapping, free-fly top-down build camera, auto-clear obstacles when building, disable collision checks option, and MORE! 👷‍♂️
 Fully-fledged Terraforming system for clearing the surface. 🧨💥
 Power system with power generation facilities. ⚡
 New constructible objects for your Outpost. 🏗️
 Radar system to scan for points of interest around you. 🌐
 Many, many more improvements, fixes and changes! 🛠️
New Gameplay Trailer
In addition to the demo update, I also have a new gameplay trailer to share, featuring footage from post-demo features in the full game! Check it out below 👇

[previewyoutube=FwB0r5f6T80;full][/previewyoutube]
As always, the game is built on your feedback, so please leave a comment or start a discussion in the Steam forum with your thoughts and constructive criticism!

Until next time, Pioneers!

notes.title: August Development Diary, Space Exploration Fest and New Demo
notes.content:
Hello, Pioneers!

Welcome to the August Development Diary for AETHUS.

This time, I have updates for you on our next Steam event participation (very soon!), a massive demo update, and sneak peeks at new mechanics and features in development.

Space Exploration Festival - New Demo
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/e254eb61ff14ffb9e4929a570f02c2f9ced00171.png

AETHUS will be taking part in the Space Exploration Fest here on Steam, starting September 2nd at 10:00AM PST (18:00BST)!

As part of the festival, I am happy to announce that a new demo will be available for the game!

This demo is a massive update, featuring new mechanics, new content, countless bug fixes, new options and settings, full keybinding support, and much more!

The demo update will go live on Friday 30th August, 10:00AM PST (18:00BST), so mark your calendars and make sure to hit those Wishlist and Follow buttons on the Steam page to be alerted when the new announcement is posted!

If your favourite content creator is yet to play the game, why not let them know that they can get early access to the new demo by getting in touch with me at hello@pawsmonaut.games!

August Development

A lot of the month has been spent preparing for the updated demo, so here's a sneak-peek at some of the new features you'll be able to enjoy! Check out the July Development Diary for some additional features including a new Scanning feature and a whole Power system!

Keybindings
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/4e6cf1d77fa9fc8377c41b74e0fb2d440bffe4b6.png
A much-requested feature that I am pleased to bring to the demo (and of course, full game) - full keybinding support for all controls in the game is now possible!

This will also allow for support for non-QWERTY keyboard layouts, so non-English-players rejoice!

Terraforming
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/a43a8ec56240f186344e6969e60ef9125c740c6e.png
[previewyoutube=K-w0SY77Ey8;full][/previewyoutube]
Terraforming was present in the original demo in a placeholder format, and I'm excited to bring the full feature to the updated demo. 

Using Terraforming Charges of different types, you can terraform the surface of the planet to clear the way for your Outpost, in an explosive way! 🧨💥

In the full game, this will be a fully featured progression system integrated with exploration and crafting, so that you can expand your Outpost over time.

Oh, and the Surface of the planet is now ~4x larger than it was in the original demo!

Build Mode Improvements
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/970326c75234a735f8c0fdf546e1ab465f21a69c.png
Making the building system in the game as easy and flexible to use as possible is a big focus of mine, and the updated demo brings several improvements, including but not limited to:

Much greater zoom.
Detached free-fly top-down build camera, or attached player camera.
Build from Storage.
Improved snapping behaviour.
Auto-clear gatherable resources if building on top of them.
Ability to disable collision checks, for the ultimate build flexibility.

I can't wait to hear how these improvements work for you, I'm always looking for feedback on ways to make this area of the game even easier to use and more powerful to create your ideal Outpost!

That's it for this development diary - as always, thanks for your support.
See you at the festival!

notes.title: AETHUS - July Development Diary
notes.content:
Greetings, Pioneers!

Summer always feels a bit slower development-wise than normal, and the Pawsmonaut Team have been trying to take a little rest here and there over the month, but work on AETHUS continues at full steam!

This month, I wanted to focus on two areas - one based on feedback from the Demo, and one entirely new feature!

Compass, Scanning and the Radar

One concern that some of you had in the Demo is being unable to always tell where you are in the world, or having a poor sense of direction.

The Compass at the top of the screen is intended to be the main navigation method through the world and aid you in discovering new points of interest, as well as finding your way back to things you've already discovered (or back to the Surface!), but I felt there was still room to improve.

One thing I've tried that is feeling good so far is the addition of a Radar.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/036cb04c872483022722f7bf0ff39b8631a80cb2.png
Pairing nicely with the Suit Scan ability (X), the Radar is a new feature that displays points of interest in the world, in small-scale, directly around the player.

As in the Demo, a tap of X will Scan the area around you and highlight resource nodes, items, and other objects of interest, but hold X for a little longer and you'll also bring up the Radar.

Points of Interest shown on the Radar are located in the exact direction they're shown around the player, just at a smaller scale, meaning you can easily know which direction to head in to find them.

The Radar will show cave entrances, Task locations, oxygen areas, Glowsticks you've deployed, datapads for unlocking new crafting plans, construction blueprints, journal logs, etc.!

[previewyoutube=PqMq_iVqDqw;full][/previewyoutube]
I feel that the addition of the Radar will really help those of you who struggled a little with navigation, but I'd be really keen to hear what you think of the feature before you get a chance to play with it yourself - drop a message in the comments below or join the Discord and provide your thoughts!

Power

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/b6ee2359ea248f750bc8303acca0d03618941631.png
In the Demo, you got a taste of one aspect of Power in the building system of AETHUS - Power Slots.

In the full game, Power has expanded to become a more feature-rich system that you will manage in order to keep your Outpost running efficiently.

Power Slots now provide Power to facilities in your habitats, drawn from an Outpost-wide pool (no need to connect things with wires!), and facilities are automatically powered if the Power value remains above zero.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/6384492f7a1907693bf3a248b4883a2ab71159bf.png
As you can see from the image above, there will be several different options for powering your Outpost (which will unlock over the course of the game) including Solar power! Different Power Generators will have different trade-offs, so choose wisely!

As Power is not intended to be a micro-management system, you don't need to worry about things like fuelling generators, using batteries because the sun isn't shining, etc.

Remember, I'd love to know your thoughts on this feature, as well as what you like or dislike in other similar games when it comes to this type of Power system!

Drop a message in the comments below or join the Discord and provide your thoughts!

Wrap-up

That's all for this devlog! 

A wee reminder that AETHUS has a Kickstarter notification page which you can sign up for with no commitment! The more followers we can get, the more likely the campaign will happen and raise some money to make the game even better!

Hope you're having a great summer, stay safe out there!

- Alex

notes.title: AETHUS Demo - Patch #10 - Now Live!
notes.content:
Patch Ten is now live!

New:

 Upon 'dying', Maeve now drops her inventory into a small crate which will persist until all contents are subsequently removed and then disappear.
 Added an interactable icon on the Vitality HUD to show that a new Journal entry has been added.
 Added a new Setting to automatically open the inventory when interacting with a Facility with an Inventory. This is the new default.
 Added a new Setting to allow holding LMB to repeatedly interact with the world rather than needing to repeatedly click.
 Added some new SFX to the Surface and Outer Caverns biomes.

Tweaks and Fixes:

 Fixed issues with interacting with things when standing very close/in front of them.
 Fixed possible duplication when dying with items picked up from crates.

notes.title: AETHUS Demo - Patch #9 - the 'Modifier Options Patch' - Now Live!
notes.content:
Patch Nine - the 'Modifier Options Patch' - is now live!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/3f8926762860783320c5aa73f2d444d37591707c.png
A lot of you requested the ability to tweak the 'difficulty' of the game - governed by the three main survival mechanics present in the Demo: Air, Vitality, and Carry Weight.

I'm happy to say you can now choose between five different options for each of these mechanics individually, making the game harder or easier in each of these areas depending on your preference.

I want you to enjoy AETHUS the way you like most, and if my 'standard' options aren't for you, then who am I to stop you playing the way you prefer?

Let me know what you think! ❤️

Oh, and I've added a few other cool new things. Take a look!

New:

 Added Modifier Options to allow for tweaking individual aspects of the survival challenge in the game to your preference.
 Options range from Easy, through Forgiving, Standard, Challenging, to Hard.
 Storage Containers (except the Makeshift Crate) now have external lights which indicate their inventory state (empty vs not empty).
 All Storage Containers can now be placed both inside and outside.
 Added a new 'Short Connector' construction which unlocks at the same time as the large one. It's a connector... but small.
 Added a sneak peek at a new feature to the 'Surface Camp' crate. This requires a new game.

Tweaks and Fixes:

 Disabled torch lights on Maeve and Roland when inside your Habitats.
 Updated a bunch of construction icons.
 Fixed potential flickering of lava in the Prologue.

notes.title: AETHUS Demo - Patch #8 Now Live!
notes.content:
Patch Eight is now live!

Some pretty big quality of life changes in this patch, as well as a few new options (and a bunch more to come!) to tweak your experience the way you like it.

New:

 Overhauled the Build Mode UX to make it quicker and easier to do anything you want.
 Modify and Terraform modes have been integrated into the 'standard' Build Mode, you can access these options by simply opening Build Mode and clicking on an appropriate object in the world. No more need to switch to a separate mode and then click. The whole experience of switching between building, modifying, and terraforming should all be smoother. Let me know what you think!
 Terraforming UX now follows the same pattern as the other modes (buttons, not double clicks).
 Added a new Settings option for triggering 'cutaways' on all Outpost buildings when one is entered, rather than just the entered building. This is the new default behaviour.
 Added a new Settings option for adjusting the sensitivity of Camera Rotation
 Added placeholders for future new settings options.
 Removed negative effects from neglecting Vitality system.
 Added the ability to remove an item from a hotbar slot by hovering it and pressing (DEL).

Tweaks and Fixes:

 Fixed Modify Mode button text sizing being inconsistent.
 Updated Power Slot graphic with new art to make its purpose clearer.
 Increased FOV multiplier slider maximum value from 1.5 to 2.0.
 Set default antialiasing value to a lower level to improve performance.
 Fixed 'jumping' Build Mode UI issues.
 Unified shader material between all Build Modes.
 Set DX11 as default renderer which may improve performance and fix(?) a crash issue for some users.
 Fixed some surface objects being terraformable when they shouldn't be.
 Fixed hotbar scrolling behaviour being incorrect if player also used keys to select slots.
 Fixed Dew Catcher having the wrong Compass POI name.
 Updated icon for Small Crate.

notes.title: AETHUS Demo - Patch #6 Now Live!
notes.content:
Patch Six - the 'Ultrawide Building Patch' - is now live!

This one's a biggie, with a bunch of requested features and improvements! Keep your feedback coming!

With these new Settings Options, ultrawide monitor users should now be able to tweak the game to be much more playable. Please let me know how these changes are for you!

New:

 Added Aspect Ratio options to Settings menu.
 Added FOV override slider options to Settings menu.
 Added ability to move constructions within themselves, so you don't need to move them far away and then back again to make a small position change.
 Added info to the notification shown when you can't build due to a collision, with the type of object causing the problem.
 Added save game persistence for build mode settings e.g. camera change and snapping.
 Added a title bar in Windowed graphics mode.

Tweaks and Fixes:

 Fixed initial splash screen still being full white.
 Fixed crates on the surface reverting to old positions after being moved or dismantled.
 Increased size of various smallest items to make them a little easier to see.
 Fixed dialogues potentially repeating when you return to the surface.
 Fixed side entrance to cave showing POI before correct time.
 Fixed Settings Options potentially not saving if changed in main menu and not going in-game.

notes.title: AETHUS Demo - Patch #5 Now Live!
notes.content:
Patch Five  is now live with more requested changes/improvements!

Thanks again to everyone who's provided feedback for the demo, I hope you feel that things are continuing to improve in the game!

New:

 Added an 'Always Run' option to the Settings Menu which allows the character to always sprint, and holding SHIFT instead causes them to walk.
 Added the ability to consume inventory items directly from the hotbar with MMB.
 Added a new notification to make it clear when mining is obstructed.

Tweaks and Fixes:

 Increased item pickup radius by about 50%.
 Fixed tasks potentially re-appearing after completion.
 Changed the build mode camera transition from linear to cubic interpolation for a smoother transition effect.
 Fixed energy being lowered even with obstructed mining requests.
 Adjusted notification for attempting to build underground before you are able.
 Toned down whiteness of title splash screen.
 Fixed deployable items activating on 'death'.
 Fixed settings sokmetimes not being accurately shown when loading game in main menu settings window.

notes.title: AETHUS Demo - Patch #4 Now Live!
notes.content:
Patch Four - the 'Camera Patch'- is now live!

Thanks so much to everyone who's provided feedback for the demo so far!

The top requests by far were more control over the game camera - so here you go!

I'm really keen to know how this is for you, so please let me know in the comments or discussions.

More to come this week.

New:

 Added a new Orbit ability to the camera which provides a lot more control over the camera positioning.
 Moved Camera control to RMB (it's also on MMB if you still want to use it)
 Removed the weight/inertia of the camera movement and made it much snappier.
 Can now use ESC to close the inventory.
 Added a Scanning tutorial to the Prologue to help make this feature clearer.

Tweaks and Fixes:

 Improved the unlock flow for the Crafting Bench to avoid potential confusion on how to construct this facility.
 Added the Dew Catcher facility unlock during the first steps of building the Outpost, without needing to explore to unlock it.

Balancing

 Tweaked the Dew Catcher time to produce water, and limited its inventory to one bottle at a time.

notes.title: AETHUS Demo is now LIVE!
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44678379/e8a3ae4720947bb4cbb7330af83cd54709049b99.png
Good day, Pioneers! The day has finally arrived!

The very first playable demo of AETHUS is now live as part of our participation in the Steam Open World Survival-Crafting Festival!

The demo features the beginning of the game and will give you 1-2 hours of gameplay in the opening areas (but is not time-limited), allowing you to mine and gather resources, build up the beginning of your Outpost on the surface of the planet, craft and refine items, and get a taste of the dystopian narrative that will drive you through the game!

It's been a year since I started full-time on the game so this is a big milestone - I really hope you like the game, and would love to hear your thoughts.

You can join the Discord channel to provide feedback and chat with myself and other players! I'd love to chat with you.

The demo will be live and playable until June 3rd at 6PM UK time (5PM UTC, 10AM PT) at which point it will become unplayable until it returns in a future event, so make sure you play before then!
